title: Initialisation-dependent fixation in noisy weighted voter models: a resolution of Conjecture 2 of Ganesh, Hauert and Valla
shortTitle: Fresh starts help the better option: Conjecture 2 resolved
oneLine: In the noisy weighted voter model, a freshly initialised swarm reaches the better decision strictly more often than Conjecture 2 of Ganesh, Hauert and Valla predicts, so the conjecture fails as stated; under the equilibrium start the source simulated, it is exact for a constant favourable rate and is replaced by a mean-quality formula otherwise.
abstract: Ganesh, Hauert and Valla (Swarm Intelligence 19(3), 2025) studied a noisy weighted voter model for best-of-n decisions in robot swarms. Their Conjecture 2 says that, on a complete graph, the probability that k agents holding the better option eventually win converges to the survival probability of a branching process built from the equilibrium distribution of the agents' signalling rates, while specifying freshly sampled initial rates. For bounded rates with every favourable rate strictly below every resident rate, this candidate proves the population limit for arbitrary initial rate laws: it is governed by the transient mean resident rate. Freshly sampled residents update faster at first, because equilibrium over-represents slow residents (the inspection paradox), so whenever resident rates vary the better option wins strictly more often and the conjecture fails as stated. With favourable rates 1/2 or 1 and resident rates 2 or 6, each with probability one half, the limit is 0.7842… rather than (3+√37)/12 = 0.7569…; with constant favourable rate 1 it is 0.70203… rather than 2/3. Under the equilibrium start that the source simulated, the conjectured formula is exact for a constant favourable rate; for varied favourable rates the limit is 1 − (E T_B/E T_A)^k, again above the conjectured value. Under these two starts the stationary formula never overestimates; its underestimate has supremum 27.3355 percentage points, not attained, and is below 8.27 points when resident rates differ by at most a factor of three. An explicit burn-in time removes the effect.

evidence: Written proofs of every theorem in a 28-page manuscript: a configuration-uniform fixation bound, an exact common-thinning coupling with a time-inhomogeneous branching process, the strict fresh-start bias, the sharp envelope and global supremum, rate-cap and burn-in bounds, random favourable rates and the equilibrium-start identity. Exact rational certificates (standard library) for the constant-rate witness to 30 digits, the global supremum bracket and the Theorem 6 identity for four laws; exact finite-population chains for N ≤ 5; floating-point multitype, large-N and rate-cap values labelled numerical; nine semantic negative controls; replay from a clean copy and in GitHub CI.

metadataProvenance: Prepared from the final manuscript (27 October 2026, 28 pages), its verification scripts and stored outputs, and the frozen release archive. The versioned GitHub and Zenodo research archives were checked against the frozen release assets on 27 October 2026.
keyResults: Corrected limit (Theorems 1 and 4): for arbitrary initial rate laws, fixation converges to survival of a time-inhomogeneous branching process whose birth rate is the transient mean resident rate b_ν(t), not its equilibrium value.

Conjecture 2 fails as stated (Theorem 2, Corollary 5): if resident rates vary, the fresh-start limit strictly exceeds the conjectured value; e.g. 0.70203… instead of 2/3 (certified), and 0.7842… instead of (3+√37)/12 = 0.7569… with varied favourable rates.

Equilibrium start (equation (7), Theorem 6, Corollary 7): the conjectured formula is exact for a constant favourable rate; for varied favourable rates the limit is 1 − (E T_B/E T_A)^k, strictly larger.

Size of the error (Theorem 3, Proposition 5.1, Section 5.4): the single-founder underestimate has supremum 27.3355… percentage points, not attained; with resident rates within a factor of three the proved ceiling is below 8.27 points.
Burn-in (Section 6): pre-ageing the residents for time τ shrinks the error like e^{−b₀τ}, with explicit single- and k-founder bounds.

narration: When the starting line matters: fixation in noisy swarm decisions. An Evidence Press briefing. First, the background. Robot swarms often choose between options, such as two nest sites, without a leader. In the weighted voter model, each robot advertises its favourite for a while, then copies a random neighbour. Better options are advertised for longer, so they spread. In 2025, Ganesh, Hauert and Valla conjectured a formula for the chance that a small group backing the better option eventually wins in a large swarm. Their formula describes the other robots as they look after a long run, in equilibrium. Yet the conjecture says every robot starts with a freshly measured quality. Now, the main finding. That difference matters, and the conjecture fails as stated. A snapshot of a long-running swarm over-represents slow robots, because slow robots keep their state for longer. This is the inspection paradox. A fresh swarm has no such bias, so its robots switch faster at first, just when a small group is won or lost. So whenever advertising rates vary, the better option wins more often than predicted. In one example, the true chance is about seventy-eight per cent, not seventy-six. The source's own simulations started in equilibrium. There, the formula is exactly right when the better option has one fixed rate, but it underestimates again when that rate varies. The worst-case gap approaches twenty-seven percentage points, and a short burn-in removes it. The limitations: the proofs cover complete networks, and only when every better-option rate is below every other rate. This is an unrefereed, AI-assisted candidate, released on twenty-seven October twenty twenty-six. The paper, proofs and checks are linked on this page. This briefing uses a synthetic AI voice, and is not additional evidence.

decisionObject.description: Status of Conjecture 2 of Ganesh, Hauert and Valla (2025) for the noisy weighted voter model: refuted as stated (fresh start) whenever resident rates vary; exact under the equilibrium start for a constant favourable rate; replaced by 1 − (E T_B/E T_A)^k under the equilibrium start for varied favourable rates.
decisionObject.scope: Complete graph, N → ∞ with k fixed, exponential signalling periods, bounded rates with every favourable rate strictly below every resident rate. Overlapping supports, including the source's Gamma-noise examples, are outside scope.

semanticBridge.description: Conjecture 2 is quoted clause by clause with page numbers (pp. 186–187), including 'with initial values of T_A and T_B sampled as above'; the paper separates the stated fresh start from the equilibrium start used in the source's Section 4.7 simulations and treats both.
remainingRisks: One may read 'sampled as above' as a drafting slip meaning the equilibrium start; the paper resolves the conjecture under both readings.
Multitype numerical values are uncertified floating point; the strict inequalities are proved separately.
The bounded literature check is not exhaustive priority certification.
